santa-cruz-c50-d213.summary: October 1630: before besieged Casale, the French and Spanish armies are about to fight when a young papal envoy, Giulio Mazarini, rides between the lines and wrests an agreement. On 6 December Philip IV answers his governor of Milan, the Marquis of Santa Cruz, in cipher: he approves the agreement, which “restored the reputation” of a discredited Emperor, wants a peace concluded before March, orders a secret inquiry into the army’s unreadiness, insists that Casale and Mantua stay guarded by the Emperor and that the Milanese be fortified — “and above all do not spend a single real badly”.
santa-cruz-c50-d213.en:
[In plain text:] Don Philip, by the grace of God King of Castile, León, Aragon, the Two Sicilies, Jerusalem, Portugal, Navarre and the Indies, etc., Duke of Milan, etc. Marquis of Santa Cruz, my cousin, of my Council of State, my lieutenant general of the sea, governor and captain general of the State of Milan.

Senator Vilani arrived with the dispatch you wrote on the 20th and ‹…› of October, at a moment when it was awaited with great concern and eagerness, since my ministers in Germany had already reported the resolution taken by the Emperor my uncle to issue the dispatches for the peace of Italy, of which copies have been sent.

system: the royal cipher “A” of Philip IV’s letters to Santa Cruz (1629–1632), also used by the Infanta in Brussels: a homophonic syllabary (letter groups pan = ca, fan = que, sol = por…, numbers 1–99 for syllables and letters) and a nomenclator (numbers 100–260 and…
